pneumatic.m: Of or relating to or using air (or a similar gas).

pneumatically.e: At the present time the transmission is very often done hydraulically or pneumatically.

pneumatics.m: The branch of mechanics that deals with the mechanical properties of gases.

pneumatophore.m: An air-filled root (submerged or exposed) that can function as a respiratory organ of a marsh or swamp plant.

pneumatophores.m: An air-filled root (submerged or exposed) that can function as a respiratory organ of a marsh or swamp plant.

pneumococcal.m: Of or derived from or caused by bacteria of the genus pneumococcus.

pneumococci.m: Bacterium causing pneumonia in mice and humans.

pneumococcus.m: Bacterium causing pneumonia in mice and humans.

pneumoconiosis.m: Chronic respiratory disease caused by inhaling metallic or mineral particles.

pneumoencephalogram.m: An X ray of the brain made by replacing spinal fluid with a gas (usually oxygen) to improve contrast.

pneumogastric.m: Of or relating to the vagus nerve.

pneumonectomies.m: Surgical removal of a lung (usually to treat lung cancer).

pneumonectomy.m: Surgical removal of a lung (usually to treat lung cancer).

pneumonia.m: Respiratory disease characterised by inflammation of the lung parenchyma (excluding the bronchi) with congestion caused by viruses or bacteria or irritants.

pneumonic.m: Pertaining to or characterised by or affected by pneumonia.

pneumonitis.m: Inflammation of the lungs; caused by a virus or an allergic reaction.

pneumothorax.m: Abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity resulting in the collapse of the lung; may be spontaneous (due to injury to the chest) or induced (as a treatment for tuberculosis).
